title: OpenClaw, Formerly Clawdbot: Demos, Risks and Q&A
summary: Nate Little demos OpenClaw, formerly Clawdbot, and explains why he gives it its own machine and accounts.

chapters.title: Q&A: An Honest Review of the Code

learn: The project went from Clawdbot to Moltbot to OpenClaw, made by Peter Steinberger. Moltbook is a separate agent social network, and ClawHub is the skills registry where malicious skills have been posted.
A gateway normalizes messages from Telegram, Discord, iMessage and WhatsApp and routes them to an agent runner such as Claude Code, Pi, OpenCode or Codex, with voice replies through ElevenLabs.

He sees it as a step beyond skills: autonomous, proactive, with cron jobs built in, which is both the appeal and the risk. His advice: give it its own machine, its own email address and its own accounts.
He has put in at least 100 hours, much of it learning, and without constant correction the agent makes a mess. He finds the engineering elegant but says the velocity causes security issues.

He describes a stray agent running an unexpected database query, defenses such as injected prompt-injection guidance, and a planned daily review of session logs that recommends fixes for his approval, implemented through pull requests.
